source: Re-baselined for the current development host on 2026-11-20, with the harness and build of a15f3c958572, on a Windows 11 x64 host with 16 logical CPUs shared with other work; the runs were pinned to four logical CPUs, at a load of 29-34% (Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage). Each figure is the median of three calibrate.py --label start runs, one after another, each a lit -j1 invocation of the test inside a Windows job object; test CPU is lit's CPU minus that of a configuration-only invocation with the same parameters. The three runs: xunit 14.84 s (the first run), 7.94 s, 7.44 s; test CPU 6.09 s (7.20 - 1.11), 5.33 s (6.53 - 1.20), 5.14 s (6.08 - 0.94); load 29%, 30%, 34%. quiet_seconds = 7.94 and test_cpu_seconds = 5.33, the medians (both from the second run). Before: quiet_seconds 11.73 (19.5 x 5.74 / 9.54) and test_cpu_seconds 5.74, from M24's harness-cost WP, 2026-10-30, on the earlier development host.
